lesson.subject: maths
lesson.title: Adding and Taking Away to 100
lesson.summary: Count on and back, cross a ten, add tens, find missing numbers and solve word problems.
learning_objectives: Add and take away by counting on and back
Add and take away across a ten
Solve word problems and find missing numbers

standards.text: Add and subtract numbers using concrete objects, number lines and mental methods

success_criteria: I can add and take away numbers within 100
I can make a ten to cross a ten
I can solve a story problem and check my answer
lesson.real_life: Counting sweets, pocket money and how many pages are left in a book.

warm_up.explanation: 43 has 4 tens, so it is bigger.

blocks.markdown: Today we add and take away numbers to 100, with tricks that make it quick.
blocks.say: Welcome back, number explorer! Today we get faster at adding and taking away. We count on and back. We cross a ten. We add tens in a snap.

blocks.alt: A big pile of ripe oranges
blocks.caption: A stall full of oranges to count.
blocks.credit: Photo by Fitri Ariningrum on Unsplash
blocks.say: Look at this pile of oranges. A stall sells them. How many are there? Let's add and take away to find out!

blocks.markdown:
To **add** a small number, start at the bigger number and **count on**.

34 + 3: start at 34, then say 35, 36, 37.
blocks.say: Here is a speedy way to add. Say we want thirty-four plus three. Do we have to count from one? No way! We start at thirty-four, and then we count on three more. Thirty-five, thirty-six, thirty-seven. The answer is thirty-seven. Watch the frog hop along the number line.

scenes.caption: Start at 34.
scenes.say: Here is a number line from thirty to forty. The frog sits on thirty-four. That is where we start.

scenes.caption: 34 + 3: hop three times.
scenes.say: Hop one. Thirty-five. Hop two. Thirty-six. Hop three. Thirty-seven. Three hops, because we are adding three.
The frog landed on thirty-seven. So thirty-four plus three equals thirty-seven.

blocks.text: Stop 2: Count back to take away

blocks.markdown:
To **take away** a small number, start at the bigger number and **count back**.

41 - 3: start at 41, then say 40, 39, 38.
blocks.say: Taking away goes the other way. To take away, we count back. Let's try forty-one take away three. Start at forty-one. Count back: forty, thirty-nine, thirty-eight. The answer is thirty-eight. The frog hops backwards, to the left.

scenes.caption: Start at 41.
scenes.say: The frog starts on forty-one, at the right.

scenes.caption: 41 - 3: hop back three times.
scenes.say: Now hop back. Forty. Thirty-nine. Thirty-eight. Three hops to the left, because we are taking away three.

question.prompt: Which sum does this say? Start at 60, then count back 2.

blocks.title: Zara and the orange stall
blocks.transcript: Zara helps at an orange stall. Today she counts the oranges. There are thirty-eight oranges. Then seven more arrive. Zara starts on thirty-eight. She hops on a number line. Hop two to forty. Forty is a friendly ten! Seven take away two leaves five. Hop five more. Forty-five oranges! She made a ten first. A shopper buys six. Hop back five to forty. Then one more. Thirty-nine left. Shukriya, Zara!
blocks.caption: Zara adds by hopping to the next ten.

blocks.say: Let us remember. To add, count on. To take away, count back. Always start at the bigger number.

blocks.markdown:
To add across a ten, make a **ten** first.

8 + 5: 8 + 2 = 10, then 10 + 3 = 13.
blocks.say: Sometimes our jump goes over a ten. Take eight plus five. We could count on five, but let's be clever. Eight needs two more to make ten. So take two from the five. Eight and two make ten. We still have three left. Ten and three make thirteen! Making a ten first is a super trick.

scenes.caption: 8 needs 2 more to make 10.
scenes.say: Here are eight dots in a ten frame. The frame has two empty spaces. We need two more to make ten.

scenes.caption: The frame is full: 10.
scenes.say: We take two from the five and fill the frame. Now the frame is full. That is ten!
Five take away two leaves three more. Ten and three make thirteen. So eight plus five is thirteen.

blocks.text: Stop 2: Take away across a ten

blocks.markdown:
To take away across a ten, go back to **ten** first.

13 - 4: 13 - 3 = 10, then 10 - 1 = 9.
blocks.say: We can cross a ten when we take away too. Thirteen take away four. First take away three to get to ten. Then take away one more. Ten take away one is nine. So thirteen take away four is nine. Try it at home with buttons.

blocks.alt: 13 take away 3 is 10. Then take away 1 more to make 9.
blocks.caption: 13 take away 3 is 10. Then take away 1 more to make 9.
blocks.say: Thirteen buttons, take away three to reach ten, then one more.

blocks.text: Stop 1: Add and take away tens

blocks.markdown:
To add or take away **tens**, change the tens digit. The ones stay the same.

34 + 20 = 54. 54 - 20 = 34.
blocks.say: Adding tens is easy once you know tens and ones. Here is thirty-four. Three tens and four ones. Now add two tens. The tens change. Three tens and two tens make five tens. But the ones stay the same! Fifty-four. Taking away tens works the same way.

scenes.caption: 34 is 3 tens and 4 ones.
scenes.say: Here is thirty-four. Three tens and four ones.
Now we add two more tens. Look at the board. Five tens now! The four ones did not change. Thirty-four plus twenty is fifty-four.

question.hint: 4 tens and 3 tens make 7 tens. The ones stay 6.

blocks.markdown:
A missing number puzzle: 7 + ? = 10. The answer is 3.

Adding and taking away are **partners**: 7 + 3 = 10 and 10 - 7 = 3.
blocks.say: Time for a number puzzle. What goes in the box? Seven plus something makes ten. Add the missing number: seven plus three is ten. We can also take away to find a missing number. Ten take away seven leaves three. Adding and taking away are partners. Warm up your brain first with a memory game.

blocks.markdown:
Solve a story problem in steps: **read**, find the clue, work it out, then check.

Clue words: altogether and more mean add. Left and fewer mean take away.
blocks.say: Word problems are stories with a number puzzle hiding inside. Here is a way to solve them. First, read the story. Second, spot the clue words. If it says more or altogether, we add. If it says left or fewer, we take away. Third, work it out. Fourth, check that the answer makes sense.

blocks.text: Stop 2: Stories with money and sweets

blocks.markdown:
Maryam has 25 sweets. Her aunt gives her 30 more. How many altogether?

25 + 30 = 55 sweets.
blocks.say: Here is one for you. Maryam has twenty-five sweets. Her aunt gives her thirty more. How many sweets does Maryam have altogether? The clue word is altogether, so we add. Twenty-five plus thirty. Two tens and three tens make five tens. Ones stay five. Fifty-five sweets. Does that make sense? Yes, it is more than we started with.

scenes.caption: Maryam starts with 25 sweets.
scenes.say: Maryam has twenty-five sweets. Two tens and five ones.

scenes.caption: 25 + 30 = 55. That is 55 sweets altogether.
scenes.say: Her aunt gives her thirty more. That is three more tens. Now there are five tens and five ones. Fifty-five sweets!

blocks.prompt: A bag of 60 stickers has 20 taken out. How many are left? Have a think first.
blocks.answer_markdown: 40 stickers are left. 60 - 20 = 40, because 6 tens take away 2 tens leaves 4 tens.
